item.text:
**Bottom Line**

Marcos was **modestly closer by the end of 2024** to the program he had been signaling at the start, but mostly on **technocratic execution, crisis management, anti-rent moves, and security coordination**. The year does **not** show clean ideological consolidation or a broadly healthier civic order: red-tagging, media pressure, and selective accountability persisted, and some flagship cost-of-living fixes only partially worked.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Title:** IMF Article IV Consultation Press Release  
  **Publisher:** International Monetary Fund  
  **Date:** December 19, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/12/17/pr-24478-philippines-imf-concludes-2024-article-iv-consultation  
  **Claim:** The IMF said the Philippines handled external headwinds well, growth stayed resilient, inflation averaged 3.2% in 2024, and fiscal consolidation was underway. This is the strongest independent sign that Marcos ended the year closer to his stability-and-growth program than he began.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** Philippine Statistics Authority 2024 Inflation Report  
  **Publisher:** Philippine Statistics Authority  
  **Date:** 2024 annual report  
  **URL:** https://psa.gov.ph/price-indices/cpi-ir/node/1684065571  
  **Claim:** Annual inflation fell to 3.2% in 2024 from 6.0% in 2023, with food inflation also easing. That supports a real year-end improvement on one of Marcos’s core revealed priorities: inflation control.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** SONA 2024 / Philippine Development Plan implementation frame  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office / NEDA  
  **Date:** July 23, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sona-highlights-whole-of-government-effort-to-achieve-food-security-inclusive-economic-growth-neda/  
  **Claim:** Marcos explicitly tied the SONA to implementing the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028 and to food security, inclusive growth, and coordinated whole-of-government delivery. This shows the program became more operationalized by midyear.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** Pag-Abot Program institutionalization  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office via PIA  
  **Date:** January 22, 2024  
  **URL:** https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2024/01/22/pbbm-issues-eo-no-52-institutionalizing-and-expanding-dswds-pag-abot-program-for-street-dwellers-other-poor-and-vulnerable-individuals  
  **Claim:** EO 52 turned anti-poverty rhetoric into a standing inter-agency program with monitoring and reporting for street dwellers and other vulnerable groups. That is concrete evidence of institutionalized delivery rather than pure slogan politics.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** New Government Procurement Act  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office  
  **Date:** July 20, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/  
  **Claim:** The procurement reform standardized forms, institutionalized e-procurement, and reduced discretion and favoritism. This supports a reading that Marcos moved the state closer to a cleaner, more rule-based governing model.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** POGO ban and enforcement follow-through  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office  
  **Date:** November 11, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-refutes-alleged-loophole-in-eo-74-reiterates-pogo-ban-in-all-forms/  
  **Claim:** Marcos closed loophole arguments around the offshore-gaming ban after already ordering the sector wound down. This is strong evidence of a corrective anti-rent move that pushed the administration closer to its stated anti-crime, public-order agenda.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

- **Title:** Flood-control response after Typhoon Carina and Habagat  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office  
  **Date:** July 26, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-calls-for-comprehensive-national-flood-control-plan-to-protect-communities-production-areas/  
  **Claim:** Marcos ordered a national flood-control plan and swift assistance after severe flooding, framing the response around protecting communities and production areas. This supports a modest year-over-year gain in crisis-management capacity and program execution.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Title:** South China Sea incident-prevention agreement with Vietnam  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office  
  **Date:** January 30, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-viet-nam-sign-agreements-on-rice-trade-agriculture-scs-incident-prevention-and-management/  
  **Claim:** Marcos secured a formal incident-prevention and management agreement plus coast-guard cooperation, which is evidence of preserving external stability through institutional channels rather than escalation.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9, 2B.7

- **Title:** Provisional arrangement and maritime communication channels with China  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / ThePrint  
  **Date:** July 21, 2024 and July 17, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.theprint.in/world/china-philippines-agree-on-provisional-arrangement-for-south-china-sea-resupply-missions-manila-says/2184146/  
  **URL:** https://www.theprint.in/world/exclusive-philippines-china-to-set-up-three-new-channels-to-handle-south-china-sea-rows-source-and-document-say/2178053/  
  **Claim:** Manila and Beijing created new maritime communication channels and then reached a provisional arrangement framed as de-escalation through dialogue and consultation. This is one of the clearest signs that Marcos improved immediate regional stability by year-end.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9, 2B.7

- **Title:** Red-tagging and civic-space pressure persisted  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** September 25, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders  
  **Claim:** HRW reported ongoing harassment, threats, and red-tagging of union leaders and other groups. This is strong counterevidence: the regime’s broader political-control environment did not clearly move toward liberalization or durable institutional restraint.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Title:** Freedom in the World 2024: Philippines  
  **Publisher:** Freedom House  
  **Date:** 2024  
  **URL:** https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024  
  **Claim:** Freedom House said elections were still distorted by disinformation, vote buying, patronage, and red-tagging. That means Marcos’s program advanced in state capacity terms, but not in a way that clearly cleaned up the broader political field.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Title:** No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it  
  **Publisher:** Presidential Communications Office  
  **Date:** November 14, 2024  
  **URL:** https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/  
  **Claim:** Marcos refused independent ICC cooperation on the Duterte drug war, allowing only tightly controlled domestic review. That is a clear limit on accountability and weakens any claim of broad institutional deepening.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10, 8B.9

- **Title:** Rice tariff cut and later partial failure  
  **Publisher:** Philippine News Agency / GMA News Online  
  **Date:** June 12, 2024 and December 10, 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1226754  
  **URL:** https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/economy/929579/neda-reduced-rice-tariffs-failed-to-lower-prices/story/  
  **Claim:** The administration made a data-based tariff cut to stabilize rice prices, but NEDA later said retail pass-through was limited. This is the clearest mixed case: Marcos was adapting policy, but the flagship relief measure did not fully deliver.  
  **Question IDs:** 8B.10

**Search Gap**

- I found strong evidence that Marcos was **closer to the economic and administrative parts** of his program by end-2024.
- I did **not** find reliable evidence that he had achieved a durable ideological consolidation or a fully cleaned-up political environment.
- The remaining gap is mainly **causality and durability**: many positive macro indicators improved by year-end, but some of that likely reflected broader disinflation and external conditions, not only domestic policy.
